transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because I’ve been feeling really restless. I don’t know if that’s the right word, but it feels like I can’t quite settle inside my own skin anymore. Like I need to jump up and do the next thing, even when I’m worn out and I know I should just sit still.
Do these feelings of restlessness ever come on as sudden attacks that peak within minutes?

I don’t think so… not like an attack, if I’m understanding you right. It’s more just sort of there, building or buzzing along, not something that suddenly peaks in a few minutes. Does that make sense?
Have you had a period where you felt unusually up or irritable for several days in a row?

I’m not sure… I don’t think I’ve had anything like being “up” for days, at least not that I’d call unusual. Irritable, maybe here and there, but I don’t know that it’s been several days in a row in a way that stands out. I could be missing what you mean, though.
Have you been worrying a lot about different parts of your life?
I don’t know… I mean, I worry some, like anybody does, I suppose. But I’m not sure I’d say it’s a lot about everything. Maybe I don’t always notice it that way. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
I’m not really sure… I mean, I have my low moments, but I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly. I try not to dwell on it. Maybe just a little down sometimes? Is that what you mean?
Did you have trouble sitting still when you were a child?

I guess… yes, probably more than I like to admit. In grade school, the teachers would say I was bright, but they’d write things like I was careless or talking out of turn. I remember needing reminders to stay in my seat and finish my work. I lost papers a lot too. I don’t know if that counts as trouble sitting still, but it was something they noticed.
Do you still often have trouble focusing on tasks?

Yes… I think I do, more than I probably let on. I can sit down with the senior center newsletter or the choir schedule and start out reading it just fine, but after a few minutes I’ll realize my eyes have gone over the same few lines and I don’t really know what I just read. It’s a little embarrassing, because it seems like it should be simple. Is that the sort of focusing you mean?
Do these focus and restlessness problems make it hard for you to manage day-to-day tasks?

Yes… I suppose they do, more than I like to admit. I try to keep up, but my family has had to help with bills and paperwork because I’ll put things down or mean to finish them and then… I don’t.

And at church, or with the garden group, there have been times people had to change plans or cover something I said I’d handle. I feel awful about that. These are people I care about, and I don’t want them thinking I’m unreliable… but I think maybe they don’t feel they can count on me the way they used to. Is that what you mean by day-to-day tasks?
Before you turned 12, were these problems with focus and restlessness already happening?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but even back in grade school, the teachers would write that I was bright, just… careless. Losing papers, talking out of turn, needing reminders to stay in my seat or finish my work.

So, yes, it was already happening before I was 12. That’s the kind of thing you’re asking about, right?
Do these problems with focus and restlessness happen in more than one part of your life, such as at home and when you’re with other people or doing activities?

Yes… yes, it’s not just at home. I wish I could say it was only with paperwork or things around the house, but it shows up other places too.

My family has had to step in with bills and forms and that sort of thing because I lose track or don’t finish them. And then at church, or with the garden group, there have been times I was supposed to handle something and someone else had to cover it or rearrange plans. I feel very embarrassed saying that, because those groups matter to me, and I don’t want to let people down.

I think… maybe people don’t feel they can count on me the way I’d like them to. Is that the kind of situation you mean?
Have you been using any alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other drugs recently?

Um… no, I don’t think so. I’m not using drugs or anything like that. I don’t… I wouldn’t want to make anything sound like it’s from that.

I mean, if you mean medicines or things prescribed, I’m not sure what all counts, but alcohol or cannabis or stimulants like you said—no, not recently. Is that the answer you needed?
Have you ever needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy the next day?

I don’t think so… not in the way you mean, I don’t believe. I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep well, of course, but then I’m usually tired the next day, not full of energy.

If you mean feeling unusually energized on very little sleep, I haven’t really noticed that. Does that answer it okay?
Do you find yourself worrying most days, even when there isn’t a clear reason to worry?

I’m not sure I’d say most days, no. I mean, I do worry about things like anyone does, but usually there’s some reason I can point to.

I haven’t really noticed myself worrying for no clear reason all the time. If that makes sense.
